findings.explanation: The newly introduced `create_postgres_query` method (lines 325–396 in the PR) builds raw SQL strings by directly interpolating user-controlled values (`key`, `value`, `jsonb_column`) via Python's `str.format()` with no parameterization. The resulting string is then passed verbatim into `cur.execute(statement)` in `postgres_meta.py` (line 275: `statement = "SELECT * FROM {} WHERE {} ".format(self.table, postgres_query_str)`). A `key` value such as `'); DROP TABLE dids; --` or a string `value` containing a single-quote would break out of the generated SQL fragment. Although `value` undergoes a `isinstance` type check, the string branch (`else` at the bottom of the try block) embeds it directly: `expression = "{}->>'{}' {} '{}'".format(jsonb_column, key, POSTGRES_OP_MAP[oper], value)`. The `key` field receives no sanitization at all in `create_postgres_query`; `_translate_filters` is called with `strict_coerce=False` so unknown keys are left as raw strings. The `LIKE` branch also embeds `key` and the wildcard-replaced `value` verbatim. None of the branches use parameterized queries or an allow-list check on `key`. This is a newly introduced code path (entire method is new in this PR) that directly results in SQL injection.

findings.suggested_fix: Replace all `str.format()` SQL construction in `create_postgres_query` with parameterized query fragments. Use `psycopg2`'s `sql` module (`psycopg2.sql.Identifier`, `psycopg2.sql.Literal`, `psycopg2.sql.Placeholder`) to safely compose identifiers and values, and pass parameters separately to `cur.execute(query, params)`. findings.explanation: The `delete_metadata` method in the new postgres plugin omits the `scope` and `name` WHERE clause entirely, meaning the UPDATE statement affects ALL rows in the table, not just the intended DID. More critically, the `key` parameter is interpolated directly into raw SQL without any authorization check verifying that the caller owns or has permission to modify the targeted DID. The API layer (`lib/rucio/api/did.py:540`) converts scope to an InternalScope but performs no permission/ownership check before invoking the core, and the plugin itself has no WHERE scope/name filter — so any authenticated user can delete a metadata key from every DID in the database.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a WHERE clause filtering on scope and name (e.g., `WHERE scope=%s AND name=%s`) using parameterized queries so the update is scoped to the intended DID. Additionally, add an authorization/ownership check (e.g., verify the issuer account owns the scope or has the appropriate permission) before executing the update, consistent with how other mutating DID operations in the API layer check permissions.

findings.explanation: The `delete_metadata`, `set_metadata_bulk`, and `get_metadata` methods in the new postgres plugin are missing any authorization/ownership check. The API-layer `delete_metadata` (api/did.py:540) and `set_metadata_bulk` callers do not verify that the requesting account has permission to modify or read the targeted DID's metadata before dispatching to the plugin. Other mutating DID operations (e.g., `set_status` at api/did.py:555) accept an `issuer` parameter and perform permission checks, but these metadata operations do not pass or verify an issuer at all.

Rucio - Scientific Data Management
==================================

Rucio is a software framework that provides functionality to organize, manage, and access large volumes of scientific data using customisable policies. The data can be spread across globally distributed locations and across heterogeneous data centers, uniting different storage and network technologies as a single federated entity. Rucio offers advanced features such as distributed data recovery or adaptive replication, and is highly scalable, modular, and extensible. Rucio has been originally developed to meet the requirements of the high-energy physics experiment ATLAS, and is continuously extended to support LHC experiments and other diverse scientific communities.

Documentation
-------------

General information, API/REST description and guides can be found in our `documentation <https://rucio.cern.ch/documentation>`_ or on our `webpage <https://rucio.cern.ch>`_.

Try it out
----------

We provide a `dockerized environment <https://github.com/rucio/rucio/tree/master/etc/docker/dev>`_ which serves both as a demo environment and a development environment. It includes all the necessary preconfigured components for multiple storage and transfers developments.

Developers
----------

For information on how to contribute to Rucio, please refer and follow our `CONTRIBUTING <https://rucio.cern.ch/documentation/contributing>`_ guidelines. We strongly recommend to use the `dockerized environment <https://github.com/rucio/rucio/tree/master/etc/docker/dev>`_ for development.

Operators
----------

To learn how to deploy and configure Rucio, consult the `documentation <https://rucio.cern.ch/documentation>`_ available online.

Getting Support
----------------

If you are looking for support, join us on our Slack `support <https://rucio.slack.com/messages/#support>`_ channel, or send an email to our public mailing list `rucio-users@googlegroups.com <mailto:rucio-users@googlegroups.com>`_.

Rucio - Scientific Data Management

Rucio is a software framework that provides functionality to organize, manage, and access large volumes of scientific data using customisable policies. Rucio - Scientific Data Management
==================================

Rucio is a software framework that provides functionality to organize, manage, and access large volumes of scientific data using customisable policies. The data can be spread across globally distributed locations and across heterogeneous data centers, uniting different storage and network technologies as a single federated entity. Rucio offers advanced features such as distributed data recovery or adaptive replication, and is highly scalable, modular, and extensible. Rucio has been originally developed to meet the requirements of the high-energy physics experiment ATLAS, and is continuously extended to support LHC experiments and other diverse scientific communities.

Documentation
-------------

General information, API/REST description and guides can be found in our `documentation <https://rucio.cern.ch/documentation>`_ or on our `webpage <https://rucio.cern.ch>`_.

Try it out
----------

We provide a `dockerized environment <https://github.com/rucio/rucio/tree/master/etc/docker/dev>`_ which serves both as a demo environment and a development environment. It includes all the necessary preconfigured components for multiple storage and transfers developments.

Developers
----------

For information on how to contribute to Rucio, please refer and follow our `CONTRIBUTING <https://rucio.cern.ch/documentation/contributing>`_ guidelines. We strongly recommend to use the `dockerized environment <https://github.com/rucio/rucio/tree/master/etc/docker/dev>`_ for development.

Operators
----------

To learn how to deploy and configure Rucio, consult the `documentation <https://rucio.cern.ch/documentation>`_ available online.

Getting Support
----------------
